newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sega, NTT to develop SegaSaturn-based videophone.
newsitem.headline: Sega, NTT to develop SegaSaturn-based videophone.

text.p: Sega Enterprises Ltd. and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp. said Friday they would jointly develop a videophone using the SegaSaturn game player and television sets.
The two companies said they will develop and produce an adaptor that will turn the SegaSaturn players into videophones when connected to telephone lines and TV sets.
The adaptor, using a microphone and a camera, will be launched on the Japanese market at a price of around 30,000 yen ($265) next spring or summer, a Sega spokeswoman said.
NTT will develop the technology and Sega will be in charge of manufacturing and sales, the two companies said.
The initial year sales target is set at 20,000 adaptors, the spokeswoman said.
The two firms said they plan to develop new applications for the videophone in the entertainment, education and medical fields.
The gadget could bring a cheap, household-use videophone for the first time to Japan, where only expensive corporate videoconference systems are available.
By the end of October, about 3.7 million SegaSaturn game players had been sold in Japan.
